# Introduction

[Motivation: AIS-based evaluation of marine closures is now routine; Brazil
combines seasonal bans, large MPAs and satellite tracking mandates. Question:
what can AIS identify, and what confounds it? Contributions: (i) a
machine-readable regulatory knowledge base including "observability
policies"; (ii) two independently measured confounders of AIS-based
evaluation (differential satellite detection; fleet AIS adoption); (iii) a
full evaluation of the 2018 Trindade/Martim Vaz MPA that fails honestly;
(iv) the 2023 shrimp-trawl calendar reform as a design robust to spatial
detection gradients. TITLE UNDER DECISION — see docs/title_and_structure_proposal.md.]

# Institutional Background

[Defesos; MPAs (Decrees 9,312 and 9,313 of 2018); PREPS satellite tracking
(VMS, not AIS) and its mandates by fishing modality; AIS carriage rules.]

# A Regulatory Knowledge Base for Fisheries

[Atomic-rule schema; provenance chain; human validation gate; the finding
that official "closure period" PDFs are full DOU pages and that the IBAMA
summary table records only the amended sardine regime; the new category of
observability mandates (`config/observability_mandates.yml`). Registry:
19 rules from 15 norms as of 2026-09-11.]

# Data

[GFW apparent fishing effort by gear and by vessel (with vessel type and
first-transmission date); AIS presence of all vessels; OISST SST; CGU
Seguro-Defeso microdata (aggregated); ICMBio polygons via WFS. Access dates
and checksums in the compendium.]

# Two Mechanisms That Confound AIS-Based Evaluation

## Differential satellite detection
[Estimand O1: cargo-vessel detection near oceanic islands declines relative
to open ocean, 2014–2024. RESULT: leads +0.27/+0.29/+0.16 (MONA), p≈0.]

## Fleet AIS adoption concentrated in designated areas
[Estimands O2–O3: vessels first transmitting after March 2018 supply 69% of
post-designation APA hours vs 26% in control; adoption is gradual and not
mandate-driven.]

# Case I: Trindade and Martim Vaz (2018) — an evaluation that fails honestly

[Rings, TWFE, event studies, SDID, exogenous-coverage corrections, SST,
pre-AIS fleet, geographic (p=0.33) and temporal placebos. RESULT: no zone
survives; estimand O4 quantifies the naive bias.]
